newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end softer, ending six days of gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end softer, ending six days of gains.

text.p: Late selling pulled Taiwan share prices down to a slightly weaker close on Monday following six straight sessions of gains, brokers said.
The index ended down 0.96 point or 0.01 percent at 8,660.76, off an intra-day high of 8,750.15.
Turnover was a brisk T$126 billion.
The index rose during most of the session on sound first-quarter economic and corporate fundamentals, brokers said.
A cabinet agency said on Monday that Taiwan's first-quarter gross domestic product growth will likely run at around 6.6 percent, up from a February forecast of 6.40 percent.

The market largely ignored a 1.1 percent gain in Taiwan's March index of leading business indicators, the seventh consecutive rise, brokers said. The index forecasts peaks and troughs in the business cycle.
"Actually the market's recent rallies already had reflected these facts," said Capital Securities manager Alex Chiu.
Financials rose 0.84 percent to support the market, with Hua Nan Bank up T$2.5 to T$125.5.
Shares in electronics firms, which have performed strongly in recent sessions, were mixed. Computer maker First International rose to T$86.5 but chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor slid T$1.5 to T$90.5.

Brokers said the market's six-year resistance at around 8,700-8,750 remains heavy. "Since the bellwether electronics (stocks) have turned weak and other industrial sectors are unlikely to lead the upswing, the index likely will enter a consolidation phase in the coming sessions," Chiu said. For Tuesday, a 8,600-8,750 range was seen. -- James Peng (5080815)
